details:
What it does: Spacefire is a browser-based 3D explorer with three layers.

1. Solar System view: planets on real orbital paths with spacecraft such as the Voyagers, Chandrayaan orbiters, Mars Orbiter Mission and Aditya-L1 at L1.

2. Mission films: each mission launches on a to-scale model of its real rocket (Saturn V, Atlas-Agena, Titan IIIE, Delta II, Atlas V, Space Shuttle, PSLV-XL, LVM3), then cruises along its transfer trajectory.

3. Surface mode: a walkable Moon or Mars landscape with the hardware placed at real scale. Users can drive the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner or Pragyan, fly Ingenuity, fire a laser at a retroreflector, trigger seismometer "moonquakes" and watch the Apollo LM ascent stage lift off.

Story mode turns each artifact into a full-screen, chaptered story with a timeline, science cards and animated numbers. A narrator voice reads everything aloud, and synthesized sound effects follow each scene, for accessibility and immersion.

Skylabs (our creative twist): two fictional repair bases, at Shackleton crater on the Moon and Arcadia Planitia on Mars, built from real NASA concepts (Kilopower, MOXIE, RASSOR, Mars Ice Home, Rodwell). Each machine has a researched failure cause and status: offline, heritage-protected, debris or out of reach. Users run a step-by-step repair in a robotic bay. Historic sites and crashed probes are deliberately left alone, which keeps the science honest.

Tools: JavaScript, three.js (WebGL), Web Audio API, Web Speech API, HTML/CSS and Node.js, with NASA 3D Resources models and hand-built procedural models for hardware missing from NASA's library (LRV, Surveyor, Pathfinder, Sojourner, Ranger, ALSEP, LRRR).

Impact: it turns little-known leftover hardware into a free, explorable public museum that runs in any browser, with no install. It teaches mission history, planetary science and the case for preserving heritage sites and building future Moon/Mars infrastructure.

Factors considered: accuracy (real coordinates, scale and dates), accessibility (narration and keyboard support), performance (compressed textures, lazy loading) and respect for heritage sites.
